text: Refactoring is the process of improving the structure of your code without changing what it does. Think of it like cleaning and reorganizing a messy room: you rearrange the furniture, but you don’t throw away any of your belongings. The main goal is to make the code more readable and easier to maintain. By breaking large functions into smaller ones, renaming unclear variables, or removing duplicate code, you reduce "technical debt"—the extra work you’ll have to do later because of messy shortcuts taken now. Good refactoring keeps the same behavior, but makes future changes simpler and safer.
